shortcut_name: product-two constraint triggers bipartite graph coloring
evidence: The solutions use a two-color array with comments such as "values are 1 or 2" and explicitly "Check if bipartite"; they assign colors by BFS.
affordance_in_statement: Each configuration code must be chosen from the set {1, 2}. An entanglement link is stable if and only if the product of the configuration codes assigned to its two endpoints evaluates to exactly 2.
secondary_shortcut_name: smallest-index component root gets color 1 for the lexicographic minimum
removal_suggestion: This is an intrinsic reduction: with endpoint values restricted to 1 and 2, product 2 means the endpoints must differ, so the task is necessarily bipartite coloring. The arithmetic wording could be re-presented as "the two endpoints must receive different codes," but the underlying shortcut cannot be removed without changing the task.
